title: The Last Garden Again
premise: Mara Villalobos, a beast-speaker whose gift is forbidden inside the valley where magic cannot follow, watches the border wards collapse on the night the stars go out — and a stranger named Ilian is pulled through the breach, carrying the last seed of the Garden that once anchored her country's existence. As the moon races toward its thirteenth turn, Mara and Ilian must cross a land that is literally forgetting itself into nonexistence, guided by animals who remember what people cannot. Along the way Mara discovers she is not valley-born at all but a fragment of the Garden's own memory given flesh, and that Ilian was sent to retrieve her, not the seed. In the climax she must choose between restoring the old country — which would erase every living person now in it — or planting the Garden anew inside herself, unmaking her identity to become the door. She chooses rebirth: the country ends, a new one begins, and Mara survives as something both herself and other, with Ilian choosing loyalty to the woman over truth of his mission.
about_author: Ulyana Brightwater is the pen name of a former field botanist who spent a decade cataloguing endangered plants before turning to fantasy full-time. Her work is known for landscapes that behave like characters and for quiet, devastating choices made in gardens.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. On the eve of the moon's first missing star, Mara secretly speaks with a dying fox beyond the ward-line, hiding her gift from the valley elders. The stars extinguish one by one and the wards shatter like glass. Emotional beat: dread and exhilaration as the world she trusted visibly breaks.

chapters.title: A Stranger Falls Through
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A man tumbles through the broken border, half-dead, clutching an iron box that hums like a hive. The valley animals flee from him; only Mara can hear him speak — and he speaks in the tongue of beasts. Emotional beat: wary fascination and fear of discovery.

chapters.title: What the Elders Remember
chapters.summary: Ilian's POV. Recovering in the elder hall, Ilian learns the valley has no memory of any country beyond its rim — maps end at the wards. He conceals the box and his mission from the Council of Roots. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Fox's Bargain
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The dying fox, recovered, tells Mara the country outside is 'unwriting itself' and that the box holds the Garden's last seed. It offers to guide them if she swears an oath in beast-tongue. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of choosing exile.

chapters.title: Leaving the Valley That Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Mara and Ilian slip past the Council's watchers at dawn; behind them the wards knit closed, sealing the valley off forever. Mara looks back once. Emotional beat: grief braided with liberation.

chapters.title: The Unwritten Road
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Outside, geography is softening — rivers run uphill, villages exist only at dusk. They meet a ferryman who cannot recall his own name but remembers his oars. Emotional beat: uncanny melancholy; wonder curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Ilian's POV. Ilian explains the moon will complete a thirteenth turn before the country finishes forgetting itself; after that, no door out exists. He lies about why he needs Mara specifically. Emotional beat: the cost of a necessary lie.

chapters.title: The City of Half-Names
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In the capital, citizens wear name-tags they rewrite hourly as memories erode. A librarian who remembers everything offers passage in exchange for the seed. Emotional beat: horror at a people politely consenting to vanish.

chapters.title: Beasts Who Remember
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Animals alone retain true memory; a parliament of crows reveals that the Garden didn't die — it was murdered by its own gardeners. Mara realizes Ilian knew. Emotional beat: betrayal's first cold shock.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Ash Orchard
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Mara demands truth; Ilian admits he was sent by the Garden's remnant order to bring back 'the vessel,' not merely the seed — and the vessel is a person. Emotional beat: trust shattered mid-journey, alliance held together by necessity alone.

chapters.title: The Moon's Second Face
chapters.summary: Ilian's POV. Haunted, Ilian dreams the Garden's death and wakes changed — the seed has rooted faintly in his blood too. He begins doubting whether returning it is mercy or resurrection of an old tyranny. Emotional beat: doubt blooming into conscience.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Farewell
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The nameless ferryman ferries them across a river of static and dissolves mid-crossing, content at last to be forgotten. Mara vows someone will remember this country. Emotional beat: tender sorrow; purpose crystallizing.

chapters.title: Hunters of the Remnant Order
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Other agents of the Garden's order arrive to take the vessel by force, revealing Ilian was meant to be expendable. A running battle through a forest that forgets them mid-fight. Emotional beat: adrenaline and the strange comfort of fighting side by side again.

chapters.title: What Mara Is
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Wounded, Mara touches the seed and experiences flashes of another life: she is a splinter of the Garden's memory, planted in a valley family generations ago. Her forbidden gift was never forbidden — it was the point. Emotional beat: identity crisis; grief for a self she thought was hers.

chapters.title: The Librarian's Price
chapters.summary: Ilian's POV. The all-remembering librarian corners them, offering to preserve the old country intact if they surrender the seed — but preservation means freezing everyone inside it forever. Ilian refuses alone, without telling Mara. Emotional beat: loneliness of leadership; loyalty outweighing truth.

chapters.title: Twelfth Turn
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. One turn remains. The land is nearly gone — they walk on sky. Mara and Ilian finally speak honestly, and forgiveness arrives not as absolution but as choice. Emotional beat: quiet reconciliation under a starless moon.

chapters.title: The Door Out of a Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The fox leads them to the threshold: a door standing free in nothing, which opens only for the Garden's memory. The hunters and the librarian converge. Emotional beat: breathless convergence, all debts coming due.

chapters.title: The Choice of Vessels
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Climax. To open the door and restore the old country, Mara must pour herself into it — erasing everyone now alive there, including Ilian. To refuse is to let the country finish dying. She chooses a third path: to plant the Garden in herself and become the new door. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into sovereignty.

chapters.title: Rooted
chapters.summary: Ilian's POV. Mara blooms into living Garden; the thirteenth turn completes and the old country exhales out of existence. Ilian holds the door as she becomes it, nearly losing himself. Emotional beat: awe, sacrifice, love stated plainly at last.

chapters.title: A New Country, First Morning
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Dawn breaks over a small, real, imperfect land grown from Mara's remembered life — the valley, the fox, the ferryman's river, all reborn slightly wrong and entirely hers. Stars return. Emotional beat: hard-won peace.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Oath
chapters.summary: Ilian's POV. Ilian chooses to stay, renouncing the remnant order, and asks the new Garden — Mara — what she wants of him. She answers: 'Remember me as I was, walk with me as I am.' Emotional beat: devotion freely given.

chapters.title: The Last Garden Again
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, epilogue. Years later, children in the new country speak to animals openly, and a fox with a familiar limp brings news of valleys beyond the hills where old wards still hold. Mara smiles, roots deep, and opens a gate. Emotional beat: hopeful, open-ended renewal.
